commitResults.messageTitle: Added new banner, changed bot name to Bibi. Updated greetings.
Implemented a new Task class, made modules to handle Task completion logic
Added functions to write a ToDo task type
Implement inherited Level 4 task types and UI testing
Save tasks to disk whenever the task list changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Level 7 requires the task list to survive between sessions. This first step
covers writing only; reading the file back follows in the next step.

Storage owns the save file and writes one line per task in the documented
T | 1 | read book format. The path is built with Paths.get("data", "bibi.txt")
so it stays relative to the project root and works on any operating system,
and the data folder is created on demand for a fresh copy of the project.

Encoding lives with the tasks themselves: Task.toFileFormat() writes the shared
type, status, and description fields, and each subclass supplies its own extra
fields through the new getSaveFields() hook. This mirrors how getDetails()
already works, so adding a task type later needs no change to Storage.

Bibi saves after every add, mark, unmark, and remove. A failed save is reported
but does not end the session, since the in-memory list is still usable.

The UI test runner now resets data/bibi.txt before each case, because saved
tasks would otherwise leak from one case into the next. It also understands a
<<restart>> marker and a "Saved data" block so later cases can exercise loading.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Load saved tasks when Bibi starts
commitResults.messageBody:
Second step of Level 7: Bibi now reads data/bibi.txt at startup, so a session
continues from where the previous one ended.

Storage.parseTask splits a line on the field separator and rebuilds the task
through the normal Todo, Deadline, and Event constructors, which means the same
validation that guards typed input also guards loaded input. A missing save
file is treated as an ordinary first run and produces an empty list rather than
an error, since the file will not exist on someone else's computer.

Bibi confirms how many tasks were restored, and stays silent when there are
none so a first run is not cluttered.

Test plan gains three cases: tasks surviving a restart, a first run with no save
file, and restoring a file written earlier.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle save file errors and corrupted data
commitResults.messageBody:
Third step of Level 7, covering the stretch goal. Before this change a single
damaged line crashed Bibi on startup with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

Loading now checks each line before trusting it: the field count must match the
task type, the status flag must be 1 or 0, and the type code must be known.
A line that fails any check is skipped with a numbered explanation while every
other task still loads, and blank lines are ignored. Storage.load returns a
LoadReport so it can hand back both the tasks and the warnings without printing
anything itself. A file that is not readable text, or a path that is not a file
at all, is reported the same way instead of ending the program.

Task text is now rejected when it contains '|', because such text would be
split into the wrong fields when read back and would silently corrupt the file.
Deadline and Event validate their times through the same helper as the
description, which also removes the duplicated blank checks.

Failed saves name the file and the kind of error, so a problem such as the data
folder being blocked by a file of the same name is easy to diagnose.

Test plan gains a corrupted-file case and a case for the rejected separator.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Level 7: Bibi saves the task list to ./data/bibi.txt after every change and
loads it again at startup, handling a missing file, a missing folder, and
corrupted content.
